newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Sept bank loans up 28.5 pct yr-on-yr.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Sept bank loans up 28.5 pct yr-on-yr.

text.p: Malaysian banks' total loans and advances grew by 28.5 percent at the end of September on an annual basis, Bank Negara said on Monday.
The year-on-year total loans and advances growth in August for the institutions was 27.5 percent, the central bank said in a statement.
The total loans excluded housing loans sold to Cagamas Bhd, the national mortgage concern.
The increase in loans was channelled mainly to the finance, insurance and business services sectors, the broad property sector and for consumption purposes.
On an annual basis, growth in total banking deposits stabilised at 23.1 percent at the end of September versus 23.2 percent at the end of August, Bank Negara said.
The bulk of the increase -- 2.8 billion ringgit or 74 percent -- was placed with the commercial banks.

Because the increase in loans outpaced that of deposits, the banking system experienced a resource gap of 3.5 billion ringgit in September compared with a gap of 538 million ringgit in August, Bank Negara said.
Thus, the loan-deposit ratio rose to 91.3 percent at the end of September, from 90.1 percent at the end of August.
The banking system's excess liquid assets showed a 0.9 percent rise at the end of September 1996 compared with a 0.7 percent gain at the end of August 1996.
Liquidity in the banking system continued to "remain ample" in September, the statement said.

Interbank rates were relatively stable, with the monthly average of the interbank rates for seven-day to six-month money traded within a range of 7 percent to 7.35 percent compared with 6.90 percent to 7.35 percent in the preceding month.
